subject: Re: Post-demo: CloudGrid econ follow-up & benchmarking ask
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@cloudgrid.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@cloudgrid.com>
Cc: CloudGrid Sales <sales@cloudgrid.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed benchmark tests

Hi Samantha / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have an actionable plan: 

1) What we heard (high-level)
   - Primary goal: quantify unit economics for your customer-facing search product (latency sensitive, 95th < 300ms target).
   - Main comparison asks: how our inference TCO (per-1M tokens) compares to your current hyperscaler endpoints and any self-managed stack.
   - Key knobs you care about: batching behavior at small/medium scale, effective cache hit rates for repeated prompts, and graceful fallbacks during peak load.

2) Proposed test matrix (short) — want to get your sign-off:
   - Baseline: run identical prompt set (attached) across three endpoints: CloudGrid current endpoint, Redwood-hosted baseline (redwood-1.3b/q4), and Redwood-optimized (dedicated pooling + caching).
   - Metrics: tokens generated, total request tokens, per-1M token cost (in USD), 95/99 latency, median latency, and observed cache hit-rate (prefix matches).
   - Batching sweep: {batch sizes 1, 4, 16, 64} to show how cost/latency curve moves.
   - Cache warmup simulation: run cold -> warm sequences to estimate hit-rate at ~0%, 50%, 80%.

3) Deliverables & timing
   - We can run an initial synthetic run (sanity) in 48–72 hours once we have your access/consent to run the promptset.
   - Full run + cleaned econ report: ~7 calendar days.

4) Asks from you
   - Confirm the baseline hyperscaler endpoint & model you want included (name/version).
   - Approve the attached promptset (we can remove any PII).
   - Accept a short test window for the synthetic runs (we suggest Tue–Thu next week).

Attachments: 20270320-cloudgrid-promptset.jsonl (prompt example set), token_econ_estimate.xlsx (estimation template).

If that looks good I’ll loop in Rishi (solutions) and Aisha (AM) to schedule the runs and lock down the test matrix.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@cloudgrid.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.m@cloudgrid.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed benchmark tests

Ben —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we lock the matrix: 

1) Hyperscaler baseline: we currently use HyperscaleX text-infer/v3 for production. Please include that exact endpoint in the baseline.
2) Model variants: can you include a quantized variant of the Redwood model and a float32 run? We want to see accuracy/quality delta vs pure econ.
3) On caching: our product uses a short-term session cache; can your warmup simulation mimic a 30–60s TTL?
4) Compliance: any logs/samples you generate for these runs must be stored in our bucket and never persisted in Redwood analytics.

We’re OK with the proposed Tue–Thu window — Rajiv and I will confirm exact times. Please make sure the promptset omits any CloudGrid customer emails; I can scrub if needed.

Samantha Li
Head of Product — Search
CloudGrid
Samantha.Li@cloudgrid.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aisha_rahman@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap + proposed benchmark tests

Forwarding CloudGrid’s replies — this is now a priority P1 for the AE team. Summary of asks:

- CloudGrid wants HyperscaleX text-infer/v3 included as the hyperscaler baseline.
- Include both quantized (q4) and float runs; TTL for cache warmup should be 30–60s.
- They require artifacts stored in their S3 and no retention on Redwood analytics.

Rishi — can you own the test-run plan? Please produce a short run-matrix doc (attached run-matrix.md) with exact commands we’ll run, cost calculation script, and the expected artifacts we’ll return to CloudGrid. Priorities: show per-1M tokens delta, batching curves, and a simulated cache-hit sweep.

Aisha — coordinate schedule + procurement approvals (they may need us to commit a short dedicated window). Marissa — tagging you for any commercial concessions; they asked about unit-cost delta — they might push for a pilot discount if Redwood shows 20–30% TCO improvement.

Ben

Attachments: run-matrix.md
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap + proposed benchmark tests

Ben / Team —

I’ll own the runs. Proposed technical plan (high level):

Test matrix (initial):
- Models: redwood-1.3b/q4 (optimized path), redwood-1.3b/float32, open-llama-7b/q4, HyperscaleX/text-infer-v3 (baseline)
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16, 64
- Token length buckets: short (avg 32 tokens), med (avg 128), long (avg 512)
- Cache warmup: simulate prefix reuse to approximate effective hit-rates at target 0%, 50%, and 80% — using synthetic warmup sequences and sequential runs.

Measurement approach:
- Capture per-request request_tokens + generated_tokens; compute normalized per-1M token cost using real infra cost model and HyperscaleX list pricing for baseline.
- Latency metrics: p50/p95/p99 including per-batch breakdown.
- Quality checks: run 500 sampled prompts and compute basic overlap/ROUGE-like heuristics to verify quantized vs float quality deviation.

Artifacts we’ll produce: raw run logs, econ workbook (per-1M calc), comparison charts, and a short slide with top-line conclusions.

ETA: initial synthetic runs in 48–72 hrs once I have the promptset and CloudGrid S3 write access (they requested we put outputs into their bucket).

Questions for Ben / Aisha: please confirm the exact HyperscaleX endpoint string and transfer credentials for the CloudGrid bucket.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap + proposed benchmark tests

Team —

This plan looks good. A few commercial & messaging points before we run: 

- Prioritize runs that highlight our cost controls (batching + cache) and the predictable fallback behavior — CloudGrid is explicitly worried about 95th percentile spikes.
- For the external deliverable, include a short appendix explaining our unified runtime (same API across hosted/dedicated/private) and the SLA-backed Dedicated offering — these are the levers they can use to hit production SLOs.
- We should be prepared to offer a 30-day pilot discount for the initial pilot window if the econ delta is within their required threshold; don’t commit further concessions without legal.

Action items: 
- Ben: push CloudGrid to confirm HyperscaleX endpoint string + grant S3 access (today).
- Aisha: draft a one-page pilot commercial (pricing bands + trial terms) we can attach to the run report.
- Rishi: prioritize short-run matrix and start synthetic runs as soon as we get S3 access.

Keep this tight — I want the initial deck in hand by next Tue.

Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
